question: Who among the following had termed the Right to Constitutional Remedy as a ‘soul of the constitution’?
solution:
The correct answer is__** B.R. Ambedkar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **B.R. Ambedkar had termed the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'soul of the constitution' because it ensures that every citizen can approach the court if their fundamental rights are violated.**

 
 
• The Right to Constitutional Remedy is enshrined in **Article 32 of the Indian Constitution** and is considered to be one of the most important fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• Vallabhbhai Patel was one of the founding fathers of the Indian Constitution and played a key role in the integration of princely states into India, but he did not term the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'soul of the constitution.'
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India and played a crucial role in shaping India's foreign policy and economic development, but he did not term the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'soul of the constitution.'
 
• Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India and played an important role in the drafting of the Indian Constitution, but he did not term the Right to Constitutional Remedy as the 'soul of the constitution.'
 
• **Hence, "B.R. Ambedkar" is correct answer.**
